A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLIP binding study and LABCLIP method. Text, equations, tables, figures, and the complete supplementary material are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original linear-probing, LABCLIP, robustness, and representation-analysis results on synthetic and real-world data, including supplementary Tables 5–6.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds conjunctive search, probe-weight alignment, CC3M training, spatial evaluation, and downstream experiments.

M1.justification: LABCLIP retains frozen CLIP encoders, a learned linear alignment matrix, contrastive training, and standard versus hard-negative batches. Identity initialization was already documented in v1. Image-side alignment and spatial-supervision experiments evaluate the existing framework; the PDFs do not establish a redesigned core algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds CC3M training, conjunctive search with colored letters and crowded CLEVR scenes, spatial tasks on What'sUp/COCO-Spatial/GQA-Spatial, CIFAR-10/100 and ImageNet classification, and additional retrieval directions on Flickr30k and COCO. These substantially extend the represented data and task requirements beyond v1.

E2.justification: The new conjunctive-search comparison adds randomly initialized CLIP controls under both probing and zero-shot evaluation (v3 Figure 5), distinct from v1's trained BoW-constrained encoders. The central CLIP, fine-tuned CLIP, and NegCLIP comparator families remain. Standard-batch LABCLIP results are retained in the appendix rather than removed.

E3.justification: New protocols include balanced conjunctive-search classification across 5–50 objects, with 800 training and 100 test images per case; held-out attribute-object pairs versus reshuffled splits; and half-training/half-testing spatial adaptation. Section 5.3 additionally compares probe coefficients using normalized embeddings. These are new evaluation designs, not evidence that the retained core experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds conjunctive-search controls, direct analysis of probe-weight alignment, image-versus-text projection placement, CC3M training to examine dataset dependence, and analyses of compositional generalization, spatial transfer, and downstream tradeoffs. The original object-count robustness study remains; v1's similarity and modality-gap analyses are retained in Appendix A.6.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed protocols, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. Averaging probe accuracy across objects is retained; the added experiments do not introduce uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Matched core probing and LABCLIP scores remain unchanged, but v3 adds substantial results. For example, Figure 6 reports CLEVR probe-weight similarity of 0.20 before alignment and 0.75 afterward; Table 11 newly reports ImageNet zero-shot accuracy of 0.56 for CLIP versus 0.46 for COCO-trained LABCLIP. CC3M, conjunctive-search, spatial, and alternate-split outcomes are also new. Conversely, v1's real-world CLIP and LABCLIP-HNB rows for ViT-B/16 and ViT-L/14 are absent from v3.

T1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds the algebraic argument u^TAv = (A^Tu)^Tv to explain equivalent projection placement for the stated inner-product score. v1 does not contain this derivation. There is no substantial new theoretical framework or theorem; the new cosine-similarity formula mainly documents an empirical analysis.

C1.justification: The central claims remain that unimodal embeddings contain binding information and linear alignment improves its cross-modal accessibility. v3 adds explicit practical contribution claims about compatibility with existing CLIP vector databases without feature re-extraction and post hoc modular use. Additional experiments mainly support the retained scientific claim rather than replace it.

C2.justification: v3 substantially qualifies applicability by distinguishing binding from held-out compositional generalization, explaining limited spatial transfer without spatial supervision, and interpreting reduced zero-shot classification as a binding-versus-object-discrimination tradeoff. It also adds explanations involving token separation versus visual crowding, object-biased training, and dataset overlap. These go beyond v1's narrower discussion of scene complexity and modality alignment.

D1.justification: v3 adds conjunctive-search encoder, sample-count, and caption details; normalized-probe instructions; learnable parameter counts; and a claimed training-speed comparison. Existing identity initialization, optimizers, hyperparameter ranges, A100 hardware disclosure, and code-access information are retained. The additions expand documentation without comprehensively changing the reproducibility specification.

R1.justification: v3 substantially develops its relationship to prior binding results: it contrasts Campbell et al.'s cross-modal search with unimodal CLIP testing and explains how Lewis et al.'s held-out-pair evaluation differs from its binding setup. Added literature on data diversity, dataset overlap, text-to-image binding, negation, and spatial reasoning broadens the positioning. LABCLIP is also explicitly positioned as diagnostic evidence rather than an attempt to outperform state-of-the-art methods.

P1.justification: The narrative is extensively rewritten and reorganized. Unimodal binding becomes a standalone Section 4 incorporating the existing object-count analysis; alignment follows in Section 5; older representation analyses move to Appendix A.6. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are reworked, dataset descriptions are condensed, and takeaway summaries are added throughout.

P2.justification: v3 changes from a two-column layout to a single-column conference format, redraws or rearranges conceptual figures, and adds conjunctive-search and probe-alignment figures. Tables gain dataset, frozen-encoder, and parameter-count information, while new tables display spatial and downstream evaluations. Standard-batch results are redistributed, and v1 Figures 5–6 are merged into appendix Figure 12.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens and qualifies v1's diagnosis. Conjunctive-search controls and probe-weight comparisons provide complementary evidence for encoded binding and misalignment, while CC3M training tests dependence on COCO. Appendix A.5 exposes poor held-out compositional generalization and downstream tradeoffs, making the conclusions more informative about applicability. Some larger-backbone comparisons are lost and uncertainty reporting remains absent, but the added diagnostic evidence and substantive limitations provide a clear overall quality gain.
